question: How are most sexually transmitted infections (STIs) mainly spread?

options.A: Sharing eating utensils or drinking cups
options.B: Unprotected sexual contact with an infected person
options.C: Direct contact with public swimming pool water
options.D: Inhalation of airborne droplets from coughing

explanation: Spot on! STIs are mostly spread through vaginal, anal, or oral sexual contact. You've got this!

question: Why are some STIs tricky because they don't show any physical signs or symptoms?

options.A: Infected people can spread the disease without knowing they have it
options.B: Laboratory tests cannot detect pathogens if symptoms are absent
options.C: The body builds permanent immunity during the latent phase
options.D: Asymptomatic infections always resolve spontaneously without treatment

explanation: Exactly! When someone has no symptoms, they feel healthy and can unknowingly pass the infection to their partners. Good thinking!

question: Which of these common STIs is caused by bacteria and can be easily cured with antibiotics?
explanation: Great job! Chlamydia is bacterial, which means standard antibiotics clear it right up.

question: What is the main difference between bacterial and viral STIs in the body?

options.A: Bacterial infections cause permanent cellular mutations, while viral infections do not
options.B: Viral infections remain in the body long-term, while bacterial infections are usually cured
options.C: Viral infections never respond to any form of pharmaceutical treatment
options.D: Bacterial infections require lifelong maintenance therapy instead of short courses

explanation: Spot on! Bacteria can usually be kicked out with medications, but viruses like HIV or herpes stay in the body for life and need long-term management.

question: How do barrier methods like condoms actually prevent STIs?

options.A: To permanently neutralize circulating viral loads in the bloodstream
options.B: To increase local mucosal immunity against parasitic invasion
options.C: To block the exchange of infectious bodily fluids during intercourse
options.D: To destroy bacterial cell walls upon contact in the vaginal canal

explanation: You got it! Condoms act as a physical shield so infectious fluids don't pass between partners.

question: A patient wants a daily pill to prevent getting HIV before any potential exposure. What is this prevention method called?
explanation: Awesome! 'Pre-exposure' simply means taking the medicine before exposure to protect yourself. Keep it up!

question: The Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine is most famous for helping prevent which major health condition?
explanation: Correct! The HPV vaccine protects against high-risk strains that can lead to cervical changes and cancer later in life.

question: Why is it best to give the HPV vaccine before a person becomes sexually active?

options.A: The vaccine changes its chemical formulation based on sexual history
options.B: Adolescent immune systems cannot process the vaccine after sexual debut
options.C: The vaccine provides the highest protection before any potential exposure to the virus
options.D: Insurance policies refuse coverage for the vaccine once a person turns eighteen

explanation: Spot on! Vaccines work best when your immune system meets the pathogen before the actual virus does.

question: What is the most reliable, go-to test used in labs to check for chlamydia and gonorrhea?
explanation: That's right! Nucleic acid amplification testing (NAAT) is super accurate at spotting the genetic material of these bacteria.

question: Why do pregnant women routinely get screened for STIs during early prenatal visits?

options.A: To eliminate common morning sickness symptoms during the first trimester
options.B: To determine the exact biological sex of the unborn infant
options.C: To prevent transmitting infections from the mother to the developing fetus
options.D: To cure congenital genetic abnormalities present at conception

explanation: Exactly! Catching and treating infections early protects the baby from complications during pregnancy and birth.

question: What important advice should you give a patient who just got antibiotics for a bacterial STI?

options.A: Double the next dose if you forget to take one pill
options.B: Stop taking the pills the moment physical discomfort disappears
options.C: Complete the entire medication course even if symptoms resolve
options.D: Share remaining medication with your partner to save money

explanation: You got it! Even if they feel better in a few days, finishing all the pills ensures the bacteria are fully wiped out.

question: What is the main goal of antiretroviral therapy (ART) for someone living with HIV?

options.A: Suppressing the viral load and protecting immune function
options.B: Stimulating the immediate production of thick mucosal barriers
options.C: Permanently killing all virus particles within the bone marrow
options.D: Preventing the development of seasonal respiratory allergies

explanation: Spot on! ART keeps the virus levels super low, which keeps the immune system strong and healthy.

question: Why is tracing sexual partners and notifying them so important after an STI diagnosis?

options.A: It punishes individuals who fail to use proper barrier protection
options.B: It proves whether the patient acquired the infection locally
options.C: It breaks the cycle of reinfection and treats exposed individuals
options.D: It provides statistical data for insurance companies to adjust rates

explanation: Exactly! Partner notification ensures everyone gets tested and treated so they don't keep passing the infection back and forth.

question: A patient is scared and hesitant to tell their partner about a new STI diagnosis. As a nurse, how should you help?

options.A: Offer support, discuss confidential partner notification options, and explore safe ways to share the news
options.B: Tell the patient that law enforcement will handle the notification process immediately
options.C: Refuse to provide further treatment until the partner arrives at the clinic
options.D: Advise the patient to end the relationship without mentioning the health diagnosis

explanation: Wonderful nursing care! Being empathetic and offering safe, confidential options helps the patient feel supported and understood.

question: Why is it so vital for a nurse to keep a non-judgmental attitude during sexual health assessments?

options.A: It reduces the financial cost of purchasing barrier methods
options.B: It encourages the patient to share accurate health history and seek care
options.C: It eliminates the need for laboratory diagnostic testing
options.D: It guarantees the patient will never contract another infection

explanation: Spot on! When patients feel safe and respected without shame, they are honest about their health and more likely to get help.

question: Which of these actions is NOT a good recommendation for nurse-led STI prevention education?

options.A: Demonstrating the correct application of barrier methods
options.B: Discussing the schedule for routine screening and follow-up tests
options.C: Instructing patients on how to use chemical disinfectants vaginally
options.D: Explaining the importance of completing prescribed antibiotic courses

explanation: You nailed it! Douching and harsh chemicals actually harm natural protective barriers and raise the risk of infection. Never recommended!
